qolFindings.title: The self-review's 'a date in any format' is still too broad: with the telephone off, a date with a two-digit year in the Telefono column is dropped with no notice
qolFindings.scenario: Probe round7/r7x.probe V, readPhone false, block 'CVC-ALLIEVI v1' / header / 'Veldor;Marta;;16;12.3.10' / 'FINE'. The result is one student with age 16, no birth date and no unread line. 'Veldor;Marta;;16;12/03/2010 16' (10 digits) behaves the same way. '12/03/10' and '120310' are shown as unread only because their digits happen to contain '2031', which matches the year pattern. V6-1's disposition says 'a date in any format there … is shown as an unread line', and V5F-4 says a date makes the line unread. Both are false for dates with a two-digit year. The listed examples (2010-03-12, 12 / 03 / 2010, 12032010) are correct. The failure needs two deviations at once: the value one column too far, and a two-digit year. The age is kept and no wrong student is saved. Round 6 rated the same kind of overstatement QoL.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Change the wording to 'a date with a four-digit year'. Alternatively, treat a D.M.YY shape (\d{1,2}[./-]\d{1,2}[./-]\d{2}) as no telephone and add '12.3.10' to the corpus.
